title: Sentinel Shield exception evidence
description: reports/exceptions.json — the governed exceptions in force for a run. It used to be two unauthenticated integers (.active/.expired): a forged zero hid every expired exception, `{}` asserted clean governance, and no count could be audited, deduplicated or attributed. It is now a versioned RECORD set; scripts/build-security-summary.sh derives the counts from the records and refuses a count-only file. An ABSENT file still means 'this project has no exceptions'.

version.description: Schema version. Only "1" is supported; consumers fail closed on anything else.

generated_at.description: When this record set was produced (informational).

active.description: OPTIONAL declared aggregate. It is never trusted as evidence: the builder derives the count from the records and fails closed when a declared aggregate disagrees with them.

expired.description: OPTIONAL declared aggregate, checked against the derived count exactly as `active` is.

exceptions.description: Every governed exception in force. Counts are derived from these records.

id.description: Stable unique identity. Duplicates are rejected: an exception you cannot name is one you cannot audit or revoke.

type.description: What kind of exception this is (e.g. vulnerability, control, policy).

approved_by.description: Approver. Must differ from owner — enforced by the builder, which JSON Schema cannot express.

created_at.description: Real calendar date (UTC), not after expires_at.

expires_at.description: Real calendar date (UTC). A record is ACTIVE while expires_at >= today and EXPIRED below it.

source.description: Which governance channel produced this exception. Recorded per-source in the summary so one exception cannot be counted twice through two channels.

status.description: OPTIONAL. When present it must AGREE with what the dates imply; a contradiction fails closed rather than letting a declared status override the calendar.

reference.description: Ticket / record the exception is tracked in.
